introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three (booklets GCE/P/2021/0595/3/C/Grp 1, Grp 2 and Grp 3). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only (the printed paper does not say how the groups are allotted).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the picture 'CornerShop' found on the desktop, Group Two Task II) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

Aucun logiciel (traitement de texte, tableur) n'a ete execute : les menus et les etapes sont donnes de memoire (Office recent) et ne sont pas testes. Les formules de tableur ont ete traduites en Python et executees sur les donnees du sujet (totaux, moyennes, calcul des frais, tri). Aucun compilateur C ou Pascal n'est disponible : les programmes du sujet n'ont pas ete compiles, leur logique a ete verifiee par une simulation Python fidele (division entiere et reste, memes entrees, memes sorties) dont les resultats sont recopies dans les corriges.
Aucun corrige officiel n'existe : les reponses sont redigees. Les repartitions de points dans les corriges (« marking idea ») sont indicatives ; les points imprimes du sujet ne sont jamais modifies.

Pascal : les entiers du programme sont declares « integer ». Sur un compilateur a entiers de 16 bits (maximum 32767, cas d'anciens Turbo Pascal ou du mode par defaut de certains compilateurs) une entree comme 45678 (Group One) provoque un depassement ; sur un compilateur a entiers de 32 bits (cas usuel, et int en C) le resultat est celui donne. Le corrige indique la sortie attendue sur une machine a entiers de 32 bits. En Pascal ISO la largeur d'affichage par defaut d'un entier est definie par l'implementation : le corrige suppose l'affichage sans blancs de tete (cas usuel).

Task III, Group One : les points imprimes (3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 10) correspondent a l'en-tete ; les questions 2, 5, 7, 9 et 10 (save, print) n'ont pas de points. Dans l'enonce 6 le sujet imprime « the number of the number of kilo bytes » (repetition) : recopie telle quelle.

Les programmes C et Pascal du sujet ont ete recopies tels qu'imprimes ; les corriges des questions 3 et 8 donnent la sortie d'une simulation Python fidele (//, %), les programmes modifies de la question 6 (C et Pascal) n'ont pas ete compiles. En C, « char c = getchar(); » est une declaration apres une instruction (C99) : accepte par les compilateurs actuels.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch either a C or Pascal program development environment, and key in the corresponding program. Compile the program. If any errors, keep correcting and compiling until all the errors are corrected.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a C or a Pascal development environment installed on the computer (an IDE with a compiler), create a new source file, key in the program of your choice **exactly as printed** and compile it (*Build* / *Compile*, often the *F9* key).

- Check every detail while typing: the semicolons, the braces `{ }` in C or `begin ... end` and the final `END.` with its full stop in Pascal, the quotation marks, `&num` in `scanf`, `%d` for each integer, `:=` (not `=`) for assignment in Pascal.
- Read the messages of the compiler. If it reports an error (for example a missing `;` or a misspelt keyword), go to the line indicated, correct it and compile again. Repeat until the compiler reports no error.

A program that compiles without error is ready to be run.

*Marking idea:* the 3 marks reward a correctly keyed program and a successful compilation (indicative split).

Use *File* > **Save As** (or *Save*) and give the source file the name **Task 3a** (the extension is added by the program: `.c` in C, `.pas` in Pascal), in the working directory. No mark is printed for this step.

questions.enonce_markdown: Run the program two times, providing 1250 as input the first time, and 45678 as input the second time. Write the output you observe each time in the spaces provided below.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The program reads a number `num` of centimetres, computes `m = num / 100` (whole metres, integer division) and `cm = num % 100` (the remainder). Trace (same logic simulated in Python):

| Input `num` | `m` = quotient | `cm` = remainder |
|---|---|---|
| 1250 | 1250 / 100 = 12 | 1250 - 1200 = 50 |
| 45678 | 45678 / 100 = 456 | 45678 - 45600 = 78 |

**C program, input of 1250:**

```
Enter number of centimetres: 1250
1250cm is equivalent to 12m and 50cm
```

**C program, input of 45678:**

```
Enter number of centimetres: 45678
45678cm is equivalent to 456m and 78cm
```

**Pascal program:** the same results, with a space before `cm` in the first part of the message: `1250 cm is equivalent to 12m and 50cm` and `45678 cm is equivalent to 456m and 78cm`.

(The typed number shown after the prompt is the echo of the keyboard. On a machine whose Pascal `integer` has only 16 bits, 45678 exceeds 32767 and causes an overflow: see the notes of the paper. With 32-bit integers, as in C, the output is the one shown.) One mark per correct output.

questions.enonce_markdown: State what the program is designed to do.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The program is designed to **convert a length given in centimetres into metres and centimetres**: it asks the user for a number of centimetres, then displays the whole number of metres (`num / 100` in C, `num div 100` in Pascal, the quotient) and the number of centimetres left over (`num % 100` in C, `num mod 100` in Pascal, the remainder). For example 1250 cm is displayed as 12 m and 50 cm.

Print the source code of Task 3a (*File* > **Print** in the program editor) and, if the supervisor asks for it, the output of the two runs; insert the print-out in the question booklet. No mark is printed for this step.

questions.enonce_markdown: Modify the program to compute the number of the number of kilo bytes (KB) and bytes (B), when given the number of bytes as input. Compile until there no errors are detected.  *[2 marks]*

questions.corrige_markdown: Use *File* > **Save As** and name the modified program **Task 3b** (a new file, so that Task 3a is not overwritten). No mark is printed for this step.

questions.enonce_markdown: Run Task 3b with an input of 5000. Write the result you observe in the space below.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trace: `kb = 5000 / 1024 = 4` (because 4 x 1024 = 4096 and 5 x 1024 = 5120 > 5000) and `b = 5000 % 1024 = 5000 - 4096 = 904`.

```
Enter number of bytes: 5000
5000B is equivalent to 4KB and 904B
```

(Result confirmed by a Python simulation: quotient 4, remainder 904; check: 4 x 1024 + 904 = 5000.) In Pascal the message shows a space before `B`: `5000 B is equivalent to 4KB and 904B`.

**Answer: 4 KB and 904 B.**
Save the file again (*File* > **Save**, or *Ctrl + S*) under the name **Task 3b**. No mark is printed for this step.
Print the source code of Task 3b and the result of the run with 5000; insert the print-out in the question booklet. No mark is printed for this step.
